correctness.rationale: All p≥4 are covered. The exact normalized p×p matrix has orthonormal same-sign columns, yielding Gram eigenvalues 1±singular values of its cross block. For the balanced two-block sign split, an L×L cross corner with L=floor(p/2) has entries, after separable diagonal phases, [p sin(pi(j+k+1/2)/p)]^{-1}; their positive denominators are checked since j+k+1/2<p. Entrywise domination of the finite Hilbert matrix divided by pi and a positive top eigenvector gives norm(C)≥lambda_max(H_L)/pi. The known de Bruijn–Wilf relation pi-lambda_max(H_L)~pi^5/(2(log L)^2), with log L/log p→1, gives the limsup coefficient pi^4/2. The finite checker passed 343 assertions across 49 periods; finite evidence is supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest accessible 2026 paper formulates a two-sided inverse-log-squared claim as Conjecture 7.5, without proving the upper half. Its Theorems 5.1 and 6.1 supply the underlying block and finite-matrix identities, and Corollary 7.3 supplies only an unquantified infimum-zero statement. The new entrywise positive finite corner comparison gives a uniform quantified one-sided upper estimate. The de Bruijn–Wilf finite Hilbert asymptotic is existing input, expressly attributed. Related older Hilbert matrix work concerns an ordinary Hilbert operator and not the binary periodic Vandermonde minimum eigenvalue.

value.rationale: The source explicitly formulates the critical inverse-log-squared periodic degeneration as a two-sided conjecture. The new all-period Hilbert-corner comparison proves its upper half and gives an explicit limsup coefficient without assuming balanced pattern extremality. This is a natural missing quantitative stability estimate for periodic Riesz systems, with useful finite-period bounds, not an arbitrary parameter substitution or table recomputation. The central unknown matching lower rate and sharp coefficient remain open.
